title: In 40 off-food moving C. elegans, neuron classes at higher connectome trophic levels had shorter activity timescales; in 8 on-food animals there was no relation
abstract: Question: in cortex, areas higher in the anatomical hierarchy have longer intrinsic timescales. Does a similar rule apply to identified neurons in the C. elegans connectome? Approach: we fitted exponential decays to the autocorrelation (lags 0.6-30 s) of NeuroPAL-identified whole-brain GCaMP traces in 40 off-food, freely moving animals (Atanas 2023, 3,548 neurons) and 8 on-food animals with little movement (Dag 2023, 814 neurons). We compared class median timescales with the trophic level of each class in the Cook 2019 chemical connectome. Results: off food, higher trophic level gave shorter timescales (Spearman rho = -0.31, 58 classes, p = 0.019; negative in 36 of 40 animals; partial rho = -0.41 after degree, cell type, animal count and label confidence). The relation remained with 800-frame windows, without heat-stimulus recordings, with other autocorrelation measures and with the Witvliet adult-8 connectome. On food there was no relation (rho = +0.09, 54 classes, p = 0.54). Most classes were slower on food (46 of 53; median ratio 1.84), and in an exploratory test the slowing increased with trophic level (rho = +0.30, p = 0.027). Strength-preserving rewired connectomes gave 82% of the off-food relation (null mean rho = -0.25), so each neuron's input-to-output synapse balance carries most of it. Class behaviour coupling explained much of it (partial rho = -0.13 after behaviour R2). Limitations: condition is confounded with data set and batch; across-class correlation only; GCaMP kinetics and single-exponential fits; the low-frequency power fraction did not show the relation; secondary tests are not corrected for multiple comparisons.

display.caption: Class median activity timescale (exponential fit to the autocorrelation at lags 0.6-30 s, log axis) against trophic level in the Cook 2019 chemical connectome. A: 58 classes in 40 off-food, moving animals (Atanas 2023). B: 54 classes in 8 on-food animals with little movement (Dag 2023). Colour and marker show the Cook cell type. Text gives Spearman rho with 95% class-bootstrap interval and the strength-preserving rewired-connectome null.

A: ratio of class timescale on food (Dag) to off food (Atanas, first 800 frames for equal length) against trophic level, 53 shared classes; dashed line shows no change. B: Spearman rho of trophic level against class log timescale in 1,000 strength-preserving rewired connectomes for each data set (histograms) and the real connectome (vertical lines).

Spearman or partial Spearman rho between trophic level and class timescale measures for each data set, with other timescale measures, controls (after |), and connectomes. Horizontal lines are 95% class-bootstrap intervals where calculated. Dag rows for 800-frame and no-heat variants are empty because they equal the primary test.

citations.reason: We reuse its Cook 2019 connectome parser, muscle-distance measure and strength-preserving rewiring code, and its data loading conventions for the same two data sets.
It found no reliable hierarchy-timescale relation across mouse cortical areas; our worm result also does not support a positive rule.
Hierarchy of intrinsic timescales in primate cortex, the tested rule.
